hints: A path can enter a cell only from above or from the left.
A trap cell has zero paths regardless of its neighbors.
The start cell has one path if it is open; otherwise the destination is unreachable.
analogy: The number of ways to reach each open square is the sum of the ways arriving from its top and left.
example: In an open 2x2 grid there are two routes to the lower-right: right-then-down or down-then-right.
correctness: Every allowed route to a cell ends with exactly one move from above or left; these cases are disjoint and cover all routes.
complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n^2) space, reducible to O(n) row storage.
algorithm: Set dp[0][0]=1 if the start is open, else 0. Scan cells row-major; for an open cell add paths from above and left modulo 1,000,000,007. A trap remains zero. Output dp[n-1][n-1].
